title: Many Young Americans Don't Visit the Doctor
paragraphs: Many young adults in the United States do not have a regular doctor, and many do not go for regular checkups, according to a new survey.
The survey was carried out for the Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center by the research company SSRS. From May 1 to 3, 2026, it asked 1,006 adults in the US about their health care.

The survey found that only about 71% of adults aged 18 to 29 have a primary care doctor. This is the type of doctor that people usually see for regular health problems and checkups. In comparison, 97% of adults aged 65 and older have one. Also, among young adults who do have a primary care doctor, only 47% had a checkup in the past year.

Young adults also often go to other places for care. When they have a health problem that is not an emergency, 36% of young adults go to an urgent care clinic first. In contrast, 68% of older adults contact their primary care doctor.
Why don't young people visit the doctor? Some experts think that many young adults may be worried about the cost. They may also not be sure how much their health insurance will pay.
Experts say that seeing a primary care doctor regularly is linked to better health and fewer visits to the hospital and emergency room.

Another survey, by the insurance company Aflac, found that 48% of Gen Z and 58% of millennials have a primary care doctor. However, this survey asked different questions, so the numbers are not the same.
